subject: blister beetle larvae
title: Hundreds of Beetle Larvae Pile Up to Impersonate One Female Bee

scenes.text: Hundreds of baby beetles team up to fake one bee.
In California's Mojave Desert, blister beetle larvae hatch, climb a plant stem, and cluster into one dark lump.
Then the lump gives off the scent of a female digger bee.
A male bee flies in to mate with it. Within two seconds, the larvae grab on.
When he finds a real female, they switch to her, and ride to her nest.
There they eat her pollen, her nectar, and her egg.

description:
The larvae of the blister beetle Meloe franciscanus cannot reach a bee's nest on their own, so hundreds of them work together to impersonate a female bee.
Masses of 120 to more than 2,000 larvae, each about two millimeters long, gather on a stem in the Mojave Desert and give off a blend of chemicals that copies the sex pheromone of the female digger bee Habropoda pallida. A male that comes close enough is covered in larvae in under two seconds; they move to a female when he mates and ride to her nest, where they feed on the pollen, the nectar and the bee's egg (PNAS, 2006). A 2018 study found that larvae in different regions tune their scent to the local bee species.
Is this the best con in the insect world? Comment below.
first_comment: Looking like a bee is not enough: in tests, a lump with no scent got ignored. The smell does the work. Which animal runs a better con than this?
